data.title: Water Flow
data.statement:
Here at Water-Generating Cells™ Corporation, we sell cells that generate water for our clients. These cells can fill any suitable area, allowing our clients to create lakes, pools, miniature waterfalls, and similar features with ease. We want our clients to be able to preview what their body of water will look like before we deliver and install the cells. That's where you come in.

You atr given the dimensions and the 2-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, which contains at least one water-generating cell {{o}}. It generates a water stream {{~}} (tilde) that initially only goes downward, but starts flooding at row [[r]] (0-based).

<<Terrain>>

When a falling stream encounters a cell, its behavior depends on the character in that cell:

{{.}} is an empty space. The stream enters it and continues downward.

{{_}} is a flat terrain. The stream spreads in two directions, left and right, on the row immediately above the terrain. In each direction, the stream continues spreading until it can continue downward again, or until the path is blocked.

{{^}} is a sharp terrain. The stream splits into two branches, which enters the cells immediately to the left and right of the terrain. Both branches then continue downward. A branch is created only if both its destination cell and the cell directly above it are empty.

{{|}} is a thin wall. It results in the same two-way split as {{^}}. An exception is that when either or both branches are blocked, the wall becomes waterlogged ({{!}}), and the stream continues downward in the unblocked branch (if any) and through the wall. If another thin wall is directly below a waterlogged thin wall, that wall also becomes waterlogged but does not split the stream.

{{#}} is a thick wall. The stream simply stops.

{{\}} and {{/}} are slopes. The stream moves to the cell immediately left of {{/}} and immediately right of {{\}} before continuing downward.

<<Obstructions>>

{{.}} is the only ordinary cell that a stream can enter. When entered by a stream, it becomes {{~}}. A thin wall {{|}} that is waterlogged becomes {{!}} and can also be traversed by a downward stream (but does not become {{~}}).

If two {{~}} attempt to enter the same {{.}} cell, both succeed and merge into a single {{~}}.

A stream cannot enter any cell containing terrain, another stream, or a water-generating cell. The boundary of the area is also treated as an obstruction. The only exceptions are empty cells {{.}} and waterlogged thin walls {{!}}, which are handled as described above.

If a stream attempts to enter an obstructed cell, that stream ceases to exist.

<<Flooding>>

If a stream reaches row [[r]], it becomes flood water, also represented by {{~}}.  Flood water attempts to spread to the four neighboring cells (up, down, left, right), entering only {{.}} cells. Flooding is limited to row [[r]] and below; flood water cannot spread above row [[r]]. Thin walls {{|}} are only waterlogged inside flood water when it's surrounded by water in at least 3 cardinal directions. However, flood water cannot permeate a waterlogged thin wall.
<<Task>>

Your task is to output the final state of the client's area after all streams have been generated by the water-generating cells and have interacted with the various features in the area.

Cell is below the flood level

Goal

Here at Water-Generating Cells™ Corporation, we sell cells that generate water for our clients. These cells can fill any suitable area, allowing our clients to create lakes, pools, miniature waterfalls, and similar features with ease. We want our clients to be able to preview what their body of water will look like before we deliver and install the cells. That's where you come in.

You atr given the dimensions and the 2-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, which contains at least one water-generating cell o. It generates a water stream ~ (tilde) that initially only goes downward, but starts flooding at row r (0-based).

Terrain

When a falling stream encounters a cell, its behavior depends on the character in that cell:

. is an empty space. The stream enters it and continues downward.

_ is a flat terrain. The stream spreads in two directions, left and right, on the row immediately above the terrain. In each direction, the stream continues spreading until it can continue downward again, or until the path is blocked.

^ is a sharp terrain. The stream splits into two branches, which enters the cells immediately to the left and right of the terrain. Both branches then continue downward. A branch is created only if both its destination cell and the cell directly above it are empty.

| is a thin wall. It results in the same two-way split as ^. An exception is that when either or both branches are blocked, the wall becomes waterlogged (!), and the stream continues downward in the unblocked branch (if any) and through the wall. If another thin wall is directly below a waterlogged thin wall, that wall also becomes waterlogged but does not split the stream.

# is a thick wall. The stream simply stops.

\ and / are slopes. The stream moves to the cell immediately left of / and immediately right of \ before continuing downward.

Obstructions

. is the only ordinary cell that a stream can enter. When entered by a stream, it becomes ~. A thin wall | that is waterlogged becomes ! and can also be traversed by a downward stream (but does not become ~).

If two ~ attempt to enter the same . cell, both succeed and merge into a single ~.

A stream cannot enter any cell containing terrain, another stream, or a water-generating cell. The boundary of the area is also treated as an obstruction. The only exceptions are empty cells . and waterlogged thin walls !, which are handled as described above.

If a stream attempts to enter an obstructed cell, that stream ceases to exist.

Flooding

If a stream reaches row r, it becomes flood water, also represented by ~. Flood water attempts to spread to the four neighboring cells (up, down, left, right), entering only . cells. Flooding is limited to row r and below; flood water cannot spread above row r. Thin walls | are only waterlogged inside flood water when it's surrounded by water in at least 3 cardinal directions. However, flood water cannot permeate a waterlogged thin wall.
Task

Your task is to output the final state of the client's area after all streams have been generated by the water-generating cells and have interacted with the various features in the area.
Input
Line 1: An integer w for the width of the grid.
Line 2: An integer h for the height of the grid.
Line 3: An integer r for the row at which water starts flooding.
Next h lines: A two-dimensional ASCII representation of the client's area, with w characters in each line.
Output
h lines: w characters for each line, showing what the two-dimensional grid will look like after the water-generating cells' effect.
Constraints
1 <= w <= 30
1 <= h <= 30
0 <= r <= h
There is going to be at least one water-generating cell o in the grid.
Waterlogged thin walls ! are not present in the initial area.
Example
Input
5
8
3
|.o.|
|...|
|...|
|...|
|...|
|...|
|...|
|___|
Output
|.o.|
|.~.|
|.~.|
|~~~|
|~~~|
|~~~|
|~~~|
|___|
